grh_2a2ed243a61aec1ac991.title: The Long Lane
paragraphs: Gladys Brooks has built a new life with her young son Jackie and plans to marry Jerry Connor after years of separation from her husband Jeffrey. A War Department telegram suddenly reports that Jeffrey, long believed lost, has been found alive in China. Jackie is thrilled to learn that his father served in the war, while Gladys is forced to face feelings she thought were over. When Jeffrey returns, crippled but changed, he tells Dr. Christian that he had left Gladys because he believed he was selfish and useless, then found purpose fighting in China and learned to live for other people. Convinced Gladys loves Jerry, Jeffrey plans to leave rather than stand in her way. Gladys overhears him, realizes she still loves her husband, and asks his forgiveness. Jerry quietly withdraws as the separated couple reunites and Jackie gets his father back.

grh_2a9a2f52bee710cde32b.title: Words at War 43-09-23 (15) They Shall Not Have Me
paragraphs: French prisoner John Hélion survives forced labor in Germany by clinging to one purpose: escape. Fellow prisoners pool maps, money, clothing, forged papers and hard-won knowledge from failed attempts, even disciplining a suspected informer to protect future plans. Hélion finally slips away in civilian disguise and travels through Germany by train, repeatedly risking exposure at inspections and among strangers. Near the border, sympathetic travelers help shield him, and he reaches freedom, dedicating his escape to the comrades whose collective effort made it possible.

grh_2aa390312b0e9acadbcd.title: Words at War 43-07-24 (05) the Ship
paragraphs: The British light cruiser HMS Artemis escorts a vital convoy through the Mediterranean while enemy aircraft, cruisers and battleships close in. Officers and ratings at every station struggle to keep the ship fighting as damage mounts and the captain balances protecting the convoy against the temptation to chase the enemy. Torpedoes, gunfire and disciplined damage control finally force the opposing force to turn away, allowing the convoy to continue. As darkness falls, the captain reflects that winning the battle is only part of the larger struggle and that preserving freedom will demand vigilance and purpose long after the shooting ends.
